meta.keyPoints: Refining and Marketing Scale:[1] BPCL operates the Mumbai, Kochi and Bina refineries with combined capacity of 35.3 MMTPA, around 14% of India's refining capacity. FY26 refinery throughput reached 41.15 MMT, implying sustained operation above nameplate capacity, while distillate yield improved to 84.54%.[1][2] Domestic petroleum-product sales rose to 54.18 MMT in FY26, giving BPCL a 27.27% market share; the network expanded to 25,323 retail outlets.[1] In LPG, BPCL had a 27.53% market share, 57 bottling plants, over 6,278 distributors and approximately 8.6 crore customer connections in FY26.[1] The wider network also includes industrial customers, aviation stations, lubricant-blending plants and city-gas geographical areas, keeping BPCL present across refining, logistics and multiple fuel-distribution channels.[3]

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Bharat Petroleum (consolidated, Rs crore). Two segments, as reported: downstream petroleum (refining, marketing, gas, petchem, lubes; Mumbai, Kochi and Bina refineries) and E&P (BPRL). Downstream revenue = domestic market sales volume x realisation and EBITDA = volume x EBITDA per tonne (the build in `dsBuild`, checked against the model in BPCL.ctx.js). E&P carries BPRL's pre-production costs (no Mozambique or Brazil output before FY29/FY31). EPS is on 427.26 cr shares outside the BPCL Trust for Investment in Shares (BPCL.patch.js). Investments (Rs30,136 cr at Mar-26 book: Petronet and IGL at equity value, Oil India at fair value, BPRL's Russian and other upstream JVs and the CGD JVs at equity value) stay inside treasury (net debt); the SOTP marks the listed stakes to the 30-Sep-2026 close less 20% and adds BPRL's non-investment E&P assets at invested value in separate lines. Valued on a sum of the parts: EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E downstream EBITDA.

segments.name: Downstream (refining & marketing)
segments._why: Revenue net of excise = domestic market sales x realisation (see dsBuild). Volume +1.5% in FY27E (Q1 domestic sales 13.62 MMT, +0.3% YoY: petrol +8%, diesel +8%, LPG −21% on supply curbs), +3% in FY28E and FY29E (FY26 +3.5%; BPCL buys ~20% of what it sells, so sales can grow ahead of its 35.3 MMTPA of refining, which only rises when Bina reaches 11 MMTPA around 2028). Realisation +22% in FY27E: Q1 revenue per tonne ~₹1.11 lakh vs ₹84,000 in FY26 (crude basket ~US$100/bbl vs ~US$70); we assume prices ease through the year; −9% in FY28E as crude normalises, +1% FY29E.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA per tonne of domestic sales (consolidated downstream EBITDA / domestic market sales): ₹4,500 (FY22), 2,261 (FY23), 8,638 (FY24), 4,862 (FY25), 7,689 (FY26); average FY22-26 ₹5,590. FY27E ₹3,600: Q1FY27 downstream EBITDA was about −₹3,900 cr (segment loss ₹5,920 cr after ~₹2,060 cr of D&A), about −₹2,800/t, even after a ₹3,134 cr marketing inventory gain, because retail prices lagged crude (implied marketing margin −₹5.4/litre) while refining earned US$17/bbl net of the export duty. Q2-Q4 need ~₹5,700/t as LPG under-recovery falls (₹510/cylinder in Q1, ₹490 July, ~₹210 expected for August) and the ₹7,594 cr compensation accrues at ₹633 cr a month to Oct-2026. FY28E ₹5,400 and FY29E ₹5,500: a little below the FY22-26 average because marketing margins stay political; the refining edge (GRM premium to Singapore) stays.

segments.name: E&P (BPRL)
segments._why: Small producing interests in India (Cauvery, Cambay); revenue ₹146-188 cr a year in FY22-FY26 (Q1FY27 ₹48 cr). The large assets are not producing: Mozambique LNG first cargo mid-2028 (FY29), Brazil BM-SEAL-11 first oil FY31; the Russian and Lower Zakum interests are equity-accounted (inside other income). We hold revenue flat.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA (result + D&A) −₹460 cr (FY22), −132, −201, −337, −414 cr (FY26): exploration write-offs and overheads. We assume −₹400 cr a year and leave Mozambique cash flows out of FY29E (first cargo mid-2028, ramp-up and debt service unknown); they sit in the invested value we add in the sum of the parts.

dsBuild._note: Downstream build: volume = domestic market sales (MMT); realisation = segment revenue net of excise per tonne; EBITDA per tonne = consolidated downstream EBITDA / that volume. Checked against the segment growth and margin above in BPCL.ctx.js.
dsBuild._throughputWhy: No guidance given. 41.15 MMT in FY26 (116% utilisation); Q1FY27 10.15 MMT. We assume ~41.5 / 42 / 42.5 MMT: Mumbai and Kochi already run above nameplate; Bina's 7.8 → 11 MMTPA expansion comes with the petchem complex around 2028.

assumptions._unallocWhy: Screener EBITDA less the sum of segment EBITDA was −₹41 cr to +₹473 cr in FY22-FY26 (exchange differences sit inside the downstream result). We assume nil.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guidance ₹25,000 cr kept after Q1 (Q1 ₹4,430 cr), possibly ₹26,000-27,000 cr: refinery and petchem ~₹11,000 cr, marketing ~₹10,000 cr, BPRL equity ~₹2,250 cr, CGD ~₹1,700 cr. FY26 ₹20,400 cr (segment capex ₹20,053 cr). The ₹1.7 lakh cr FY24-FY29 plan peaks in FY28-FY29 (Bina ₹49,800 cr, ₹5,900 cr spent by Jun-26; Mumbai PRFCC ~₹14,000 cr to Sep-2029; Brazil ~US$1.2bn over 3-4 years). We model ₹26,000 / 30,000 / 30,000 cr. The Andhra refinery (~₹95,000 cr) is not sanctioned and not included.
assumptions._depWhy: D&A ₹7,856 cr in FY26 (5.8% of average gross block of ₹1,34,650 cr; ₹7,257 cr and 5.8% in FY25); Q1FY27 ₹2,069 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once while most of the next three years' spend (Bina) sits in CWIP until ~2028, so we use 5.4%: ~₹8,300 / 9,800 / 11,400 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: BPCL is a net borrower at group level (borrowings incl. leases ₹54,424 cr at Mar-26 vs cash ₹17,761 cr), so interest income is in the other-income line below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: FY26 other income before exceptional items ₹4,810 cr (AR note 59): interest income ₹1,862 cr, other income ₹1,427 cr (dividends incl. Oil India, other), share of JV and associate profit ₹1,511 cr (Petronet, IGL, CGD JVs, upstream JVs), fair-value gain ₹10 cr. TTM to Jun-26 ₹4,904 cr before exceptional items (Q1FY27 ₹1,650 cr: other ₹1,249 cr + JV share ₹401 cr; the ₹1,885 cr FCTR gain left out). FY27E ₹4,800 cr (interest ~₹1,700 cr as cash is used, other ~₹1,500 cr, JV share ~₹1,600 cr), then +~4% a year.
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost ₹2,953 cr FY26 (₹3,591 cr FY25), incl. ~₹800 cr on leases; Q1FY27 ₹627 cr. Standalone debt rose from ₹10,480 cr to ₹17,396 cr in Q1 on losses and working capital; FY28-29E rise as capex is debt-funded (group debt/equity guided to peak below 1x) and interest on Bina stops being capitalised.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 tax ₹8,948 cr = 25.7% of PBT (₹34,791 cr); FY25 26.6%. Statutory 25.17%; BPRL's overseas losses get no tax shield and JV profits are post-tax. 26% throughout.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Payout 29% of consolidated PAT in FY26 (₹17.5/share, ₹7,592 cr), 32-48% in earlier years (Screener). DIPAM's CPSE guideline asks for 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher: 4% of ~₹1 lakh cr of equity (~₹4,000 cr) binds in FY27E, hence 40%; 30% after.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at rf + beta x ERP; BPCL carries ₹54,424 cr of debt incl. leases, so we set beta so that the rate equals our WACC: cost of equity 12.5% (beta 1.0), post-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (7.3% x (1−25.2%)), debt 30% of capital at the 30-Sep-2026 market value → WACC ~10.4%; beta 0.65 gives 10.4%.
dcf._tgWhy: 4%, below the house 5-6% range: Indian fuel demand grows ~3% a year now, but EVs, CNG/LNG trucks and ethanol cap petrol and diesel growth over the long run, and BPCL's prices are partly set by the Government.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 5.5%: Screener-basis margins were 9%, 6%, 2.3%, 10%, 6%, 9% in FY21-FY26 (average 7.0%); we use a lower mid-cycle because marketing margins are capped by policy in high-crude years and the new capacity is lower-margin petrochemicals.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex was 4.0%, 2.2%, 1.8%, 2.1%, 3.4% and 4.3% of net revenue in FY21-FY26 (Screener fixed assets purchased; average 3.0%); the ₹1.7 lakh cr plan lifts it in FY27-FY29. We fade to the six-year average of 3.0%, above depreciation (2%), for the rest of the period.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The Gulf disruption keeps refining margins high while crude settles near $75: BPCL's complex refineries keep their GRM premium, marketing margins recover to the FY24/FY26 level, the Government compensates the ₹15,800 cr LPG buffer, Bina and Mozambique start on time; the market pays the stock's own median multiple again.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Crude stays above $90 with retail prices frozen into state elections, LPG losses are only partly compensated, Bina slips and upstream is impaired again; earnings stay near trough levels (FY23/FY25) and the stock trades at its lower-quartile multiple.

cover.headline: The best refiner of the three, priced for it: HOLD
cover.lead: Bharat Petroleum runs three complex refineries (35.3 MMTPA, 116% utilised) and sells 27% of PSU fuel through India's most productive pump network. It earned ₹25,843 cr in FY26, then lost ₹1,873 cr in Q1FY27 (₹3,962 cr standalone) as crude hit US$100/bbl and retail prices lagged. Its own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA (after taking out its investments) has a median of 4.5x since Apr-2021, and oil marketers and refiners trade 15.7% below their five-year medians. On 4x Sep-28E downstream EBITDA of ₹31,338 cr, less net debt, plus BPRL's upstream at invested value and the Petronet, IGL and Oil India stakes at market less 20%, we get **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** The street (median ₹348; ₹350 for the four notes after Q1) uses 5.5-6.5x. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Downstream EBITDA per tonne sold in India was ₹2,260 in FY23 and ₹8,640 in FY24. The difference was not volume or efficiency but whether retail prices kept up with crude and how wide refining cracks were. In Q1FY27 BPCL's refineries earned US$41.4/bbl before the special export duty (US$17.0 after it), yet the group lost money because marketing lost ~₹5.4/litre. We forecast ₹3,600/t in FY27E and ₹5,400-5,500/t after, a little below the FY22-26 average of ₹5,590.

arguments.h: A better refiner and retailer than its peers
arguments.p: Mumbai, Kochi and Bina have Nelson complexity of 9.8-11.8, run 116% of nameplate and process 76% high-sulphur crude; BPCL's GRM has beaten Singapore's for four years (US$11.74 in FY26) and Bina earned US$56/bbl in Q1. Its pumps sell 139 KL a month each, the most of the three PSU marketers. That is why it has usually traded at a higher multiple than IOC.

arguments.h: From cash machine to builder again
arguments.p: Net debt was only ~₹6,500 cr at Mar-26 after counting investments. Now ~₹1.7 lakh cr of capex is planned to FY29 (Bina petchem ₹49,800 cr, Mumbai PRFCC, Kochi polypropylene, Brazil and Mozambique upstream, CGD), with an Andhra refinery (~₹95,000 cr) in pre-project work. Free cash flow turns negative: ₹−6,981 / −9,165 / −5,462 cr in FY27-29E on our numbers.

arguments.h: Valuation: the street's method, a derived multiple
arguments.p: The street adds investments to 5.5-6.5x EBITDA. BPCL's own history says the market pays ~4.5x for the operating business once investments are taken out (5.5x if they are left in), and the sector trades below its averages. 4x gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, of which ₹39 a share is upstream at book; the stock at ₹303 prices ~4.5x FY28E core EBITDA. Cross-checks: P/E ₹170, DCF ₹207.

flags.k: Accounting (inventory gains, LPG compensation timing, one-off FCTR gain)

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): marketing margins after the May-June price rises, LPG under-recovery (~₹210/cylinder expected for August), GRM net of the export duty, debt after the Q1 jump.
Government decisions: retail prices, SAED and export duties, compensation for the ₹15,804 cr negative LPG buffer (the ₹7,594 cr package ends in Oct-2026).
Projects: Bina petchem and refinery expansion (30.7% complete; 2028), Kochi polypropylene (May-2028), Mozambique LNG first cargo (mid-2028), Andhra refinery decision.
Crude and the Strait of Hormuz: each US$10/bbl moves BPCL's working capital and marketing margin.
Board appointments: independent directors and a reconstituted Audit Committee.

sections.title: India's third-largest refiner and second-largest fuel marketer, majority-owned by the state

blocks.p: Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) is a Maharatna public-sector company: the Government owns 52.98%. It runs three refineries with 35.3 MMTPA of capacity (Mumbai 12, Kochi 15.5, Bina 7.8; ~14% of India) that processed 41.15 MMT in FY26 (116% utilisation), 3,962 km of pipelines, and sells through 25,485 fuel stations, 6,279 LPG distributors, 2,625 CNG outlets and 81 aviation stations (Jun-2026). In FY26 it sold 54.18 MMT in India, 27.27% of PSU sales (petrol 29.8%, diesel 29.9% of PSU retail). Its upstream arm BPRL holds stakes in 15 blocks in six countries, including 10% of Mozambique LNG Area 1 and 40% of Brazil's BM-SEAL-11.

blocks.p: Two things make BPCL different from a private refiner. First, it is short of its own product: it refines ~41 MMT but sells ~56 MMT, so ~20% of what it sells is bought from other refiners and imports. Second, its retail prices for petrol, diesel and household LPG are, in practice, decided with the Government. When crude spikes the state can ask the three PSU marketers (IOC, BPCL, HPCL) to hold prices and absorb the loss, and compensates them later, partly or not at all. Downstream is therefore one business with two margin pools: a refining margin set by global cracks and a marketing margin set in Delhi. BPCL does not report them separately.

sections.title: A growing fuel market with administered prices, hit by the 2026 Gulf war

blocks.p: India's refining capacity is ~258 MMTPA; BPCL's three refineries (Mumbai 12, Kochi 15.5, Bina 7.8 MMTPA) are ~14% of it and ran at 116% utilisation in FY26 (41.15 MMT). BPCL sold 54.18 MMT in India in FY26, 27.3% of PSU sales, and needs more product than it refines: ~80% of the fuel it sells comes from its own refineries. Petroleum product demand grows ~2.5-3.5% a year; BPCL's domestic sales grew 3.5% in FY26 (petrol +5.7%, diesel +1%, jet fuel +11.4%) and 0.3% YoY in Q1FY27 (LPG −21% on supply curbs; petrol +8%, diesel +8%). India imports most of its crude (and much of its LPG and LNG), so the rupee and the Gulf matter as much as demand.

US-Iran conflict from end-Feb 2026: Strait of Hormuz disrupted. The Government cut SAED on petrol and diesel by ₹10/litre on 27-Mar-2026 and re-imposed export duties; retail prices were raised in tranches only from the second half of May. BPCL's crude premium over the Indian basket widened from US$4-5/bbl to >US$15/bbl; landed crude reached Brent + US$10-12 in May.

Petrol and diesel are formally deregulated but in practice priced by the three PSU marketers with the Government's consent; household LPG is regulated and its losses are compensated case by case (₹7,594 cr approved for BPCL in Oct-2025, paid in 12 monthly instalments from Nov-2025).

sections.title: Downstream: all of the EBITDA, a strong refining arm and a political marketing arm

blocks.p: The downstream segment refines crude (41.15 MMT in FY26 at 116% of nameplate), moves it through BPCL's pipelines and sells it (54.18 MMT in India and 1.54 MMT exported in FY26). Its EBITDA is the sum of a refining margin (GRM: product value less crude cost, US$/bbl), a marketing margin (retail price less the refinery-gate price, taxes and dealer commission, ₹/litre), inventory gains or losses and the gas, petchem and lubricants businesses, less operating costs. BPCL reports GRM every quarter (US$11.74/bbl in FY26) but never the marketing margin; brokers back it out (PL: −₹5.4/litre in Q1FY27 vs +₹5.8 in Q4FY26).

blocks.h: Refining: complex, full, and taxed when it booms

blocks.p: Mumbai (12 MMTPA, Nelson 9.84, 134% utilised in FY26), Kochi (15.5 MMTPA, 11.22, 113%) and Bina (7.8 MMTPA, 11.76, 95%) process 76% high-sulphur crude over an API range of 24-60. Distillate yield was 84.5% in FY26. BPCL's GRM has been above the Singapore benchmark for four years: US$20.2 (FY23), 14.1, 6.8, 11.7 (FY26). In Q1FY27 the war pushed cracks to multi-year highs: GRM US$41.4/bbl before the special export duty and road cess (Bina US$56, Kochi US$39, Mumbai US$34) and US$17.0 after it. The state took most of the windfall, as with the 2022 windfall tax. Spot crude rose to 69% of purchases and Russian crude to ~38% of imports, at premiums of >US$15/bbl over the Indian basket (US$4-5 before the war).

blocks.h: Marketing: the most productive network, the least control over price

blocks.p: BPCL's 25,485 fuel stations sold 139 KL a month each in FY26 (157 KL in Q1FY27), the most of the three PSU marketers; management targets a 32% retail share from ~30%. But in Q1FY27 retail prices lagged crude until the second half of May: the implied gross marketing margin fell to −₹5.4/litre (PL) and LPG under-recovery reached ~₹510/cylinder (₹5,380 cr gross, ₹3,485 cr after ₹1,898 cr of compensation). LPG losses eased to ₹490 in July and ~₹210 expected for August. The negative LPG buffer rose from ₹12,319 cr (Mar-26) to ₹15,804 cr (Jun-26), and the ₹7,594 cr compensation package ends with its October-2026 instalment.

blocks.callout: **Our forecast:** downstream EBITDA of ₹19,797 / 30,587 / 32,088 cr (₹3600 / 5400 / 5500 per tonne). FY27E assumes Q2-Q4 average ~₹5,700/t after Q1's ~−₹2,800/t: falling LPG losses, retail prices that roughly cover cost, refining margins well above pre-war levels but taxed. FY28-29E sit ~2-3% below the FY22-26 average of ₹5,590/t. Each ₹500/t is ~₹2,832 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~₹4.9 of EPS; ~₹27 a share of value at 4x).

sections.title: Upstream and new projects: ₹1.7 lakh cr of bets, none earning yet

blocks.p: BPRL, the 100% upstream subsidiary, has spent two decades building a portfolio of 15 blocks in six countries. Its segment lost ₹414 cr at EBITDA in FY26 and held ₹33,101 cr of assets at Mar-26: ₹16,259 cr in equity-accounted JVs (Russia's Vankor and Taas fields, Lower Zakum in the UAE) and ~₹16,633 cr of other assets, mostly Mozambique (₹17,648 cr of non-current assets there; ₹12,428 cr of capital work 'temporarily suspended' at Mar-26). BPRL's own equity is only ₹5,335 cr: the rest is funded mostly by debt, inside group borrowings (group debt excluding leases ₹43,482 cr vs ₹10,480 cr at the standalone company).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** BPCL has the best refining and retail assets of the three PSU marketers, and nobody will take its volumes. But a moat that does not let you set prices does not earn steady excess returns: ROE was 22%, 4%, 42%, 17% and 29% in FY22-FY26 (average ~23%), well above the cost of equity on average, but with one year in five close to zero.

sections.title: EBITDA of ₹11,000-44,000 cr: two good years, two bad ones, and a loss in Q1FY27

blocks.p: BPCL's revenue follows the crude price (₹2.3 lakh cr in FY21, ₹4.7 lakh cr in FY23, ₹4.6 lakh cr in FY26, net of excise), so revenue growth says little. What matters is the margin per tonne, and it swings with refining margins (GRM) and with how far the Government lets retail prices follow crude. EBITDA was ₹19,137 cr in FY22, ₹10,899 cr in FY23 (retail prices held after the Ukraine war), ₹44,082 cr in FY24 (crude fell, prices did not), ₹25,401 cr in FY25 (GRM fell to US$6.8/bbl) and ₹41,202 cr in FY26 (GRM US$11.7). Profit went ₹11,682 → 2,131 → 26,859 → 13,337 → 25,843 cr. FY23 was a trough, FY25 a half-trough, and Q1FY27 (a loss) starts another.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** BPCL has no "normal" year to forecast from; the right base is a cycle average. Over FY22-FY26 downstream EBITDA averaged ~₹5,590 per tonne sold in India (₹2,260 in FY23, ₹8,640 in FY24). We forecast ₹3,600/t for FY27E (Q1 was about −₹2,800/t), then ₹5,400/t and ₹5,500/t: a little below the five-year average, because the 2026 war showed again that marketing margins are a policy decision.

sections.title: A ₹1.7 lakh cr capex plan starts as cash is squeezed; ROE 4-42% with the cycle

blocks.p: Over FY24-FY26 BPCL generated ₹1,10,383 cr of operating cash and spent ₹44,147 cr on capex and ₹21,415 cr on dividends; over FY21-FY23 ₹56,257 cr, ₹25,407 cr and ₹20,689 cr. For three years capex was modest (₹8,000-10,000 cr) and net debt fell to ₹6,527 cr at Mar-26 (after counting investments at book). That is changing: "Project Aspire" plans ~₹1.7 lakh cr over FY24-FY29 (refineries and petchem ₹75,000 cr, upstream ₹32,000 cr, gas ₹25,000 cr, marketing ₹20,000 cr), led by the ₹49,800 cr Bina refinery expansion and petchem complex (2028). FY27 capex is guided at ₹25,000 cr, against FY26's ₹20,400 cr. A 9 MMTPA refinery-petchem complex in Andhra Pradesh (~₹95,000 cr) is in pre-project work. Management says group debt/equity will peak below 1x. Returns follow the cycle: ROE 4% in FY23, 42% in FY24, 17% in FY25, 28% in FY26.

sections.title: Earnings quality: inventory gains, compensation timing, impairments and a one-off FCTR gain

blocks.p: The accounts are audited by C&AG-appointed firms and are unqualified, but five items make reported profit a poor guide to the run-rate: (1) **inventory gains and losses**: BPCL carries ~₹53,000 cr of inventory, so a big crude move swings profit by thousands of crores (marketing inventory gain ₹3,134 cr in Q1FY27; BPCL stopped disclosing refinery inventory effects years ago); (2) **LPG compensation**: the ₹7,594 cr approved in Oct-2025 is booked in monthly instalments while the ₹15,804 cr negative buffer is not on the balance sheet; (3) **upstream impairments**: ₹1,774 cr (FY25) and ₹4,349 cr (FY26) at standalone level; (4) **one-offs**: a ₹1,885 cr FCTR gain in Q1FY27 consolidated profit; a ₹3,783 cr after-tax exceptional gain in FY21; (5) Screener adds **exceptional items** to other income. We also use BPCL's own share count (427.26 cr, excluding the 6.59 cr treasury shares in the BPCL Trust for Investment in Shares).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Bharat Petroleum (consolidated, Rs crore). Two segments, as reported: downstream petroleum (refining, marketing, gas, petchem, lubes; Mumbai, Kochi and Bina refineries) and E&P (BPRL). Downstream revenue = domestic market sales volume x realisation and EBITDA = volume x EBITDA per tonne (the build in `dsBuild`, checked against the model in BPCL.ctx.js). E&P carries BPRL's pre-production costs (no Mozambique or Brazil output before FY29/FY31). EPS is on 427.26 cr shares outside the BPCL Trust for Investment in Shares (BPCL.patch.js). Investments (Rs30,136 cr at Mar-26 book: Petronet and IGL at equity value, Oil India at fair value, BPRL's Russian and other upstream JVs and the CGD JVs at equity value) stay inside treasury (net debt); the SOTP marks the listed stakes to the 30-Sep-2026 close less 20% and adds BPRL's non-investment E&P assets at invested value in separate lines. Valued on a sum of the parts: EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E downstream EBITDA.

segments.name: Downstream (refining & marketing)
segments._why: Revenue net of excise = domestic market sales x realisation (see dsBuild). Volume +1.5% in FY27E (Q1 domestic sales 13.62 MMT, +0.3% YoY: petrol +8%, diesel +8%, LPG −21% on supply curbs), +3% in FY28E and FY29E (FY26 +3.5%; BPCL buys ~20% of what it sells, so sales can grow ahead of its 35.3 MMTPA of refining, which only rises when Bina reaches 11 MMTPA around 2028). Realisation +22% in FY27E: Q1 revenue per tonne ~₹1.11 lakh vs ₹84,000 in FY26 (crude basket ~US$100/bbl vs ~US$70); we assume prices ease through the year; −9% in FY28E as crude normalises, +1% FY29E.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA per tonne of domestic sales (consolidated downstream EBITDA / domestic market sales): ₹4,500 (FY22), 2,261 (FY23), 8,638 (FY24), 4,862 (FY25), 7,689 (FY26); average FY22-26 ₹5,590. FY27E ₹3,600: Q1FY27 downstream EBITDA was about −₹3,900 cr (segment loss ₹5,920 cr after ~₹2,060 cr of D&A), about −₹2,800/t, even after a ₹3,134 cr marketing inventory gain, because retail prices lagged crude (implied marketing margin −₹5.4/litre) while refining earned US$17/bbl net of the export duty. Q2-Q4 need ~₹5,700/t as LPG under-recovery falls (₹510/cylinder in Q1, ₹490 July, ~₹210 expected for August) and the ₹7,594 cr compensation accrues at ₹633 cr a month to Oct-2026. FY28E ₹5,400 and FY29E ₹5,500: a little below the FY22-26 average because marketing margins stay political; the refining edge (GRM premium to Singapore) stays.

segments.name: E&P (BPRL)
segments._why: Small producing interests in India (Cauvery, Cambay); revenue ₹146-188 cr a year in FY22-FY26 (Q1FY27 ₹48 cr). The large assets are not producing: Mozambique LNG first cargo mid-2028 (FY29), Brazil BM-SEAL-11 first oil FY31; the Russian and Lower Zakum interests are equity-accounted (inside other income). We hold revenue flat.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA (result + D&A) −₹460 cr (FY22), −132, −201, −337, −414 cr (FY26): exploration write-offs and overheads. We assume −₹400 cr a year and leave Mozambique cash flows out of FY29E (first cargo mid-2028, ramp-up and debt service unknown); they sit in the invested value we add in the sum of the parts.

dsBuild._note: Downstream build: volume = domestic market sales (MMT); realisation = segment revenue net of excise per tonne; EBITDA per tonne = consolidated downstream EBITDA / that volume. Checked against the segment growth and margin above in BPCL.ctx.js.
dsBuild._throughputWhy: No guidance given. 41.15 MMT in FY26 (116% utilisation); Q1FY27 10.15 MMT. We assume ~41.5 / 42 / 42.5 MMT: Mumbai and Kochi already run above nameplate; Bina's 7.8 → 11 MMTPA expansion comes with the petchem complex around 2028.

assumptions._unallocWhy: Screener EBITDA less the sum of segment EBITDA was −₹41 cr to +₹473 cr in FY22-FY26 (exchange differences sit inside the downstream result). We assume nil.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guidance ₹25,000 cr kept after Q1 (Q1 ₹4,430 cr), possibly ₹26,000-27,000 cr: refinery and petchem ~₹11,000 cr, marketing ~₹10,000 cr, BPRL equity ~₹2,250 cr, CGD ~₹1,700 cr. FY26 ₹20,400 cr (segment capex ₹20,053 cr). The ₹1.7 lakh cr FY24-FY29 plan peaks in FY28-FY29 (Bina ₹49,800 cr, ₹5,900 cr spent by Jun-26; Mumbai PRFCC ~₹14,000 cr to Sep-2029; Brazil ~US$1.2bn over 3-4 years). We model ₹26,000 / 30,000 / 30,000 cr. The Andhra refinery (~₹95,000 cr) is not sanctioned and not included.
assumptions._depWhy: D&A ₹7,856 cr in FY26 (5.8% of average gross block of ₹1,34,650 cr; ₹7,257 cr and 5.8% in FY25); Q1FY27 ₹2,069 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once while most of the next three years' spend (Bina) sits in CWIP until ~2028, so we use 5.4%: ~₹8,300 / 9,800 / 11,400 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: BPCL is a net borrower at group level (borrowings incl. leases ₹54,424 cr at Mar-26 vs cash ₹17,761 cr), so interest income is in the other-income line below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: FY26 other income before exceptional items ₹4,810 cr (AR note 59): interest income ₹1,862 cr, other income ₹1,427 cr (dividends incl. Oil India, other), share of JV and associate profit ₹1,511 cr (Petronet, IGL, CGD JVs, upstream JVs), fair-value gain ₹10 cr. TTM to Jun-26 ₹4,904 cr before exceptional items (Q1FY27 ₹1,650 cr: other ₹1,249 cr + JV share ₹401 cr; the ₹1,885 cr FCTR gain left out). FY27E ₹4,800 cr (interest ~₹1,700 cr as cash is used, other ~₹1,500 cr, JV share ~₹1,600 cr), then +~4% a year.
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost ₹2,953 cr FY26 (₹3,591 cr FY25), incl. ~₹800 cr on leases; Q1FY27 ₹627 cr. Standalone debt rose from ₹10,480 cr to ₹17,396 cr in Q1 on losses and working capital; FY28-29E rise as capex is debt-funded (group debt/equity guided to peak below 1x) and interest on Bina stops being capitalised.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 tax ₹8,948 cr = 25.7% of PBT (₹34,791 cr); FY25 26.6%. Statutory 25.17%; BPRL's overseas losses get no tax shield and JV profits are post-tax. 26% throughout.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Payout 29% of consolidated PAT in FY26 (₹17.5/share, ₹7,592 cr), 32-48% in earlier years (Screener). DIPAM's CPSE guideline asks for 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher: 4% of ~₹1 lakh cr of equity (~₹4,000 cr) binds in FY27E, hence 40%; 30% after.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at rf + beta x ERP; BPCL carries ₹54,424 cr of debt incl. leases, so we set beta so that the rate equals our WACC: cost of equity 12.5% (beta 1.0), post-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (7.3% x (1−25.2%)), debt 30% of capital at the 30-Sep-2026 market value → WACC ~10.4%; beta 0.65 gives 10.4%.
dcf._tgWhy: 4%, below the house 5-6% range: Indian fuel demand grows ~3% a year now, but EVs, CNG/LNG trucks and ethanol cap petrol and diesel growth over the long run, and BPCL's prices are partly set by the Government.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 5.5%: Screener-basis margins were 9%, 6%, 2.3%, 10%, 6%, 9% in FY21-FY26 (average 7.0%); we use a lower mid-cycle because marketing margins are capped by policy in high-crude years and the new capacity is lower-margin petrochemicals.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex was 4.0%, 2.2%, 1.8%, 2.1%, 3.4% and 4.3% of net revenue in FY21-FY26 (Screener fixed assets purchased; average 3.0%); the ₹1.7 lakh cr plan lifts it in FY27-FY29. We fade to the six-year average of 3.0%, above depreciation (2%), for the rest of the period.
